## Question 1 (Populations and Parameters)

a) Give a relatively simple example of a population you might want to study (in your own work) and a parameter of interest. Be sure to clearly define what the population is and what the parameter is in your answer.

b) Identify the population and parameter of interest in the following example: *I am studying the side-effects of a new drug that will be prescribed to older adults (aged 70+) with high blood pressure. I want to know how safe it is for anyone who might be prescribed this drug in the future. I recruit 10 older adults with high blood pressure to take a 50mg dose of the new drug and report on how many headaches they experience.*

## Question 2 (Samples and Statistics)

a) In your own words, describe what "statistical inference" is and why it is so important in the social and behavioral sciences.

b) Why is the size of a sample important to statistical inference? Be specific in your answer.

## Question 3 (Estimation and Uncertainty)

Use this information to answer the following questions.

> I am studying the side-effects of a new drug that will be prescribed to older adults (aged 70+) with high blood pressure. I want to know how safe it is for anyone who might be prescribed this drug in the future.
>
> I recruit 10 older adults with high blood pressure to take a 50mg dose of the new drug and report on how many headaches they experience that day. Here are their responses: `0, 4, 2, 1, 1, 0, 1, 3, 1, 0`.

a) Use R to estimate the average number of headaches experienced in this population. Print it.

b) Use R to estimate the standard error of that average (assume an infinite population). Print it.

c) In one or two sentences, explain what the standard error tells us that the average alone does not.
